newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Demirel begins coalition search talks.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Demirel begins coalition search talks.

text.p: Turkish President Suleyman Demirel began talks with opposition leaders on Thursday in a bid to find a replacement for Necmettin Erbakan, pushed into resigning as prime minister by an army anti-Islamist campaign.
Demirel went into a meeting at the presidential palace with main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz, the head of the conservative Motherland Party.
The president was to meet three other opposition figures later in the day before nominating a leader who would try to forge a new coalition government from the splintered parliament.

Parliamentary sources say Demirel might appoint a prime minister designate before the end of the day. Analysts say the main contenders are Yilmaz or Erbakan's conservative coalition partner Tansu Ciller.
Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader, quit on Thursday under a plan to hand over power to U.S.-trained economist Ciller and deflect military criticism.
Erbakan on Wednesday asked the president to give Ciller the task of forming a government so she could set up a coalition that would include the Islamists.
But Demirel, a veteran politician, has given no clues as to how he will deal with the government crisis.
